The rational-box density and bounded transverse projection argument in [L1]'s step 1.2 proves that $\mathfrak h_T$ is separable: it constructs a countable dense set in the ambient complex $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ and maps it by the bounded projection $M_{P_T}$ onto a countable dense subset of its range. current_producer_1_2_literal: 1.2 By [F10] at $p=2$, the real-valued scalar space $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ has a countable dense set $D$. It is nonempty because this scalar $L^2$ space is nonempty and $D$ is dense. By [F12], $D\times D$ is at most countable; [F14] supplies a surjection from $\mathbb N$ onto this nonempty product. Composing with $(d,e)\mapsto d+ie$ and applying [F14] again shows that $D_{\mathbb C}:=\{d+ie:d,e\in D\}$ is at most countable. For every complex scalar $u\in L^2$, its real and imaginary parts $u_R,u_I$ belong to real $L^2$, and $\|u-(d+ie)\|_2^2=\|u_R-d\|_2^2+\|u_I-e\|_2^2$; density of $D$ therefore makes $D_{\mathbb C}$ dense in complex scalar $L^2$. By two applications of [F12], $D_{\mathbb C}^3$ is countable and dense in $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, since each of three components can be approximated with squared error below $\varepsilon^2/3$. For $n\in S^2$ and $z\in\mathbb C^3$, put $a=\sum_j n_jz_j$. Using [F13] and the reality of $n_j$, direct expansion gives $\|P_T(n)z\|^2=\sum_j|z_j-n_ja|^2=\sum_j|z_j|^2-|a|^2\le\|z\|^2$, and $(I-nn^T)^2=I-nn^T$. Thus $M_{P_T}$ is a bounded idempotent on the ambient vector-valued $L^2$ space. Its image of $D_{\mathbb C}^3$ is countable and dense in its range: for $z=M_{P_T}z$ choose $w\in D_{\mathbb C}^3$ close to $z$, and $\|M_{P_T}w-z\|_2\le\|w-z\|_2$. [A1, F2, F10, F12, F13, F14]
